title: This suitcase-sized spacecraft could hear the universe before stars existed

beats.caption: This suitcase-sized spacecraft could hear the universe before stars existed
This reshapes what we know about the early universe.
beats.detail: A new mission targets the cosmic dark ages.
beats.narration: This small satellite could fundamentally change how we understand the very beginning of time.

beats.caption: It is a suitcase-sized satellite called CosmoCube.
beats.detail: Small enough to fit in a suitcase.
beats.narration: It is called CosmoCube, and it is only about the size of a suitcase.

beats.caption: It uses the Moon to block Earth’s noise.
beats.detail: Earth is too loud for radio signals.
beats.narration: Earth is incredibly noisy with radio signals, so it hides behind the Moon for silence.

beats.caption: It hunts for signals before the first stars.
beats.narration: It is searching for faint signals from a time before the first stars even existed.

beats.caption: This helps explain how dark matter built galaxies.
beats.detail: Connecting the dots of cosmic history.
beats.narration: This data could finally show us how dark matter helped build the very first galaxies.

beats.caption: It listens for the universe's oldest echoes.
beats.detail: Turning the Moon into a radio shield.
beats.narration: By turning the Moon into a shield, we can hear the oldest echoes of the universe.
